Len Marchant was behind Parlett of Dorking over the half-mile stage, but Jack Frost pulled up a little, and then Dicky Dumbrill almost caught his man over the first 220.

In the final event of the competition, the 1 Mile Medley Relay, Parlett of Dorking gave his team a winning lead, but by finishing third, we managed to score sufficient points to retain our position at the head of the league table.

Len Herbert found Parlett's finishing powers too good for him in the 1 Mile, and the times on a sodden track were all on the slow side. George Powell won the Javelin event, but in the rest of the field events we were only represented by L.

Paul's A.C., and John Parlett turned out for the latter club in the one mile and medley relay. We made a good start when Frank Craft won the 100 yards match event, and then Ian Badiali was first home in the 880, while Bill Lucas finished third in the one mile, after being content to amble in behind…
By now it was 1950 and the English middle distance scene was dominated by such 'greats[illegible] as Nankeville, Parlett, Eyre, and the young Bannister.
